pairs.subject: proactive-nudges
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/companion/proactive/triggers.rs:72-80 swallows every evaluator error with unwrap_or_default(), so a proactive system that has gone dark is spelled exactly like a quiet week.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/companion/proactive/triggers.rs:72-80 calls each evaluator as `.unwrap_or_default()` with no log and no counter, so 'did not run' and 'ran, found nothing' produce identical records and a broken evaluator silences its concern permanently; collect_all is also a hardcoded call list with no registry and no per-kind disable, and two evaluators deliver directly (proactive/execution_review.rs:887-888, proactive/message_triage.rs:427-428) instead of returning candidates.

src-tauri/src/companion/proactive/budget.rs:245 keys the daily reset on Utc::now(), not the user's local midnight, so a user well east or west of UTC gets the reset mid-day and one half of their day double allowance; caps are compile-time constants (:23, :41-47) rather than data the user may edit, and refusals are only tracing lines (proactive/mod.rs:432, :442), never counted per kind per day. The claim itself is exemplary: atomic global+per-kind check-and-decrement in one transaction with rollback (:204-241), consented lane exempt from its per-kind cap but not the global ceiling (:34-36).

src-tauri/src/companion/proactive/mod.rs:128 returns early from evaluation during quiet hours, so a candidate noticed inside a quiet window is destroyed rather than deferred - contradicting the module's own contract three hundred lines later at :392 ('Quiet hours suppress delivery, not noticing') - and no queue row ever carries a deferral reason, which lives only in tracing output. The rest of the pipeline is a model implementation: sweep before dedup (:271-277), per-kind refusal continues while only the global ceiling breaks the pass (:437-445), idempotent delivery claim (:574-584), per-kind expiry with a deliberately generous window for the no-re-fire scheduled lane (:196-210).

src-tauri/src/companion/proactive/mod.rs:549 deliver_now marks and emits with no quiet check and no budget claim, and five call sites use it (companion/night_shift/mod.rs:597, proactive/execution_review.rs:888, proactive/message_triage.rs:428 and :453, proactive/rollup.rs:58), so the quiet-crossing privilege is a function any author may call rather than a closed enumerated priority class, and crossings are neither counted nor labelled in the delivery record. The window arithmetic itself is exemplary: proactive/quiet.rs:17-56 pins inclusive/exclusive edges, the midnight wrap, the degenerate equal-endpoint case and DST behaviour in prose backed by property tests, evaluated against the local wall clock at :111-118.

src-tauri/src/companion/proactive/mod.rs:278-293 drops a re-noticed candidate whose (trigger_kind, trigger_ref) is already live instead of superseding it, so a queued card's payload is never refreshed when the story moves and no times-noticed counter accrues for cap tuning; the one-day queued expiry (:210) bounds the staleness but does not restore the 'current state of the story, once' property. The key itself is correct - kind plus subject ref, no text, no timestamp, persisted across restart, with the state-predicate cooldown the technique prefers.

src-tauri/src/companion/proactive/budget.rs:83-87 aggregates only status IN ('engaged','dismissed'), so 'ignored' - the majority outcome and the strongest negative signal - never reaches the adaptation loop; and it could not be added safely, because proactive/mod.rs writes 'expired' for both an ignored delivered card and a queued row that never won a slot, collapsing an efficacy outcome and a queue statistic into one spelling. budget.rs:73-75 also raises a well-engaged kind's cap by +1 (clamped to base+2), which the technique forbids outright, and no per-kind kill switch exists anywhere in the module.

pairs.registryProposal: efficacy-feedback states 'Nothing raises a kind's volume' without qualification. This repo implements a bounded counter-case worth considering: budget.rs:64-78 moves a per-kind cap by at most +/-1, requires >=5 engaged+dismissed samples over 30 days, clamps to base+2, and sits under an unchanged global ceiling - so total contact cannot rise, only its mix. The technique's real target is escalation on ignore (louder because unread); raising on an explicit positive action is a different act. Proposal: narrow the rule to 'nothing raises a kind's volume in response to non-action, and no adaptation may raise total contact', which keeps the anti-pattern forbidden while admitting the measured bounded-uplift form.

ActiveHoursSection constrains when an automation may execute, not when the machine may address the user; the promise being kept is an operational one, not the attention promise this technique governs.
No nudge identity is minted in this context; trigger rows carry user-authored identity and their executions are a history, not repeated news.

pairs.registryProposal: Coverage question, and a routing one rather than a hole. This pair looks like a technique-shaped resonance: the matcher joined on the word 'trigger', but proactive-nudges owns machine-initiated contact while this context is user-authored automation. Its real governors look like alerting (threshold rules and their lifecycle), scheduling/cooldown-and-debounce (rate limits, active hours), and hitl-approval (the auto / dry-run / approval unattended modes at TriggerModeBadge.tsx:18-31). pairs.registryProposal: Coverage question. Four of six techniques fail their precondition because the subject owns the durable key-value settings store while this context is credential management that merely lives under features/settings/. The match reads as directory-vocabulary rather than precondition: the material here is governed by credential-vault, and only the two surface-shaped techniques (settings-audit-and-history, save-experience) genuinely reach it. Either narrow the pairing to those two or route the context to credential-vault.

pairs.evidence: src/lib/analytics/activation.ts:125-127 writes the fire-once latch before the emission, so every milestone reached while telemetry is off is permanently consumed and never reported - a missing row in the funnel's denominator, per installation, forever.

Activation is otherwise defined from completed actions rather than visits (ACTIVATION_FUNNEL at :30-35), and the reachability discipline is visibly applied (navCatalog.ts:72-84 removes an unreachable tab from the ignored denominator).

src/lib/analytics/sink.ts:21-35 types action, category and label as bare strings with no registry the emit door validates against - label?: string is precisely the free-form payload field the technique forbids - and no entry anywhere declares an event's question, payload contract, version, or retirement; the emitted names ('view', 'tab_switch') also do not follow one object_action past-tense grammar.

src/lib/analytics/navCatalog.ts:109-124 keeps TAB_DIMENSIONS as a hand-maintained list with no gate - the axis an exhaustiveness check cannot see, which the technique names by hand ('a guard that forces every value of a declared dimension to be listed does nothing about which dimensions are declared'). The section axis is genuinely derived (:60 from NAV_SECTIONS) and each dimension's value set is a compile-error-on-omission Record (:69), and the file's own header records that the previous list tracked only 6 of ~16 dimensions - the same failure one level up remains open.

There is no allowlist at a single admission door: src/lib/analytics/sink.ts:30-35 lets any call site attach an arbitrary category/action/label string that src/lib/sentry.ts sets as a Sentry tag, and src/lib/analytics/index.ts:162 re-exports the raw trackFeature/trackInteraction helpers so a caller can emit outside the consent-switched sink entirely. Identity handling is right - no account id, and a locally minted random install id (activation.ts:52-60).

src/lib/analytics/index.ts:38 and :43 transmit every section and tab visit immediately through the sink to Sentry.captureMessage in addition to the beforeunload session summary (:149), so the collector receives a timestamped per-interaction stream - the behavioural trail the aggregate exists to prevent - and there is no counter checkpoint for abrupt death, no maximum accumulation window for a desktop session that runs for days, and no loss-rate instrumentation.

src/lib/analytics/index.ts:162 re-exports trackFeature and trackInteraction from the Sentry module beside the safe interface - the exact bypass the technique names, where the natural import is the unswitchable door and every call site that takes it sits outside the consent switch. The seam itself is well drawn (sink.ts:70-118: one contract, a real null sink for opt-out, one composition point) but no development sink exists, so the layer cannot be observed where a developer sits.

None of the twelve paths in this context is a form: there is no field registry, no submit attempt, and no summary to render. The form-level machinery exists in the same directory (FormErrorContext.tsx, FormErrorSummary.tsx) but sits outside this context's paths and is imported by none of them.

No file here owns a submit state machine, an in-flight guard, dirty tracking, or an exit path; DesignInput.tsx:120-123 raises Enter to a parent-supplied onSubmit and holds no lifecycle state of its own.
No control in this context performs or receives a commit against a system of record, so there is no rejection to route onto a field.
